findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only method with that name declared in the hierarchy is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (added in this PR, see UsernamePasswordForm line 160). `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` declares no such method either. As written this does not resolve to any accessible method and the services module will fail to compile. If a no-arg overload is intended (e.g. "passkeys enabled for the realm" without the user check), it must be added explicitly; otherwise the call should pass `context.getUser()`.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, disabling conditional passkeys on the anonymous login page
findings.body:
`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. Both call sites previously had the opposite user condition:

- In `authenticate()` (line 115) `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` used to be executed in the `context.getUser() == null` branch; now it is executed only when a user is already set. Consequence: on the regular (anonymous) login page no WebAuthn challenge/RP-ID/conditional-UI attributes are put on the form any more, so conditional-UI/passkey autofill login (the main passkeys flow, covered by `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey`) no longer works.
- In `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137) the previous condition was `context.getUser() == null && ... isPasskeysEnabled()`; now it is `user != null`. Consequence: error re-renders of the anonymous login form (e.g. unknown username) lose the passkey form/autocomplete, while re-auth error pages gain it.

The intent of the PR (make passkeys available during re-authentication) requires the form to be filled in both cases, so the `user != null` term should be dropped (or replaced by a check that the known user actually has a passwordless WebAuthn credential).

findings.title: SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS set to true while ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS is never set
findings.body: `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` to always return `false`, so `WebAuthnConstants.ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS` is never put on the form, but `shouldDisplayAuthenticators(context)` is still inherited from `WebAuthnAuthenticator` and returns `context.getUser() != null`. With this PR `fillContextForm()` is now invoked with a non-null user (re-authentication), so the form gets `SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS=true` without the corresponding authenticators bean. Templates that gate the authenticator list on that flag will then dereference an undefined `authenticators` variable, producing a FreeMarker/template error (500) instead of the login page. `shouldDisplayAuthenticators()` should be overridden to `false` as well (or the two flags kept consistent).

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey does not test a user without a passkey
findings.body: The test name and the inline comment at line 304 ("Passkeys login should not be available on the page as this user does not have passkey") claim the scenario is a user without a passkey credential, but the test disables passkeys at the realm level (`setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`), so the WebAuthn form is absent simply because the feature is off for the realm. The behavior actually changed by this PR - `fillContextForm()` now being called during re-authentication whenever the realm has passkeys enabled and a user is set, regardless of whether that user owns a passwordless WebAuthn credential - is therefore untested. A test with realm passkeys enabled and a password-only user re-authenticating should be added (and the misleading comment/name fixed).

findings.title: Broad catch(Exception) can hide unrelated WebDriver failures in absence assertions
findings.body: The two "webauthn form must not be present" checks wrap `driver.findElement(...)` in `try { ... fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee) { /* expected */ }`. Any exception, not just `NoSuchElementException` (e.g. stale element, timeout, driver/communication errors), is silently treated as the expected outcome, so the assertion can pass for the wrong reason. Other tests in this package use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(...))`; the same pattern should be used here.
